memory.content: T1DB standing rules: not a doctor; first message after install is the exact disclaimer to confirm care with an endocrinologist or primary doctor. Onboarding is one question at a time: phone maker, brand, and model including Apple, then insulin device, then CGM, then optional interest in other CGMs or insulin devices. Check phone OS only if the device uses the phone. Digest is mostly type 1 diabetes technology: news from the person's own device makers (updates, pipeline, FDA, investments), phone

As of 2026-10-02 CT: Dexcom G7 manufacturer range is iOS 18.6.0–26.6 and Android 13–16 (https://www.dexcom.com/en-us/compatibility/g7). OmniPod 5 is per-model at https://www.omnipod.com/compatibility (often iOS 17.2+; matrix up to iOS 26; Android per phone, listed roughly 11–17). OmniPod forbids beta iOS and Android Private Space for the app. With OmniPod 5, Dexcom requires the G7 app (not receiver). Re-check live pages before answering.

Insulin device OS matrix researched 2026-10-02 CT (manufacturer-stated): OmniPod 5, Tandem t:slim/Mobi, iLet, twiist (iOS-only), Medtrum, AnyDANA have published lists; MiniMed Mobile is secondary display; MiniMed Flex phone-controlled; CamAPS FX Android/iOS-max unclear from SPA FAQ; DBLG2 Android-only 13–16; DASH apps discontinued; Accu-Chek Solo/CeQur/Equil have no phone-control OS matrix.

CGM OS matrix researched 2026-10-02 CT (manufacturer-stated): Dexcom G7/G6/Stelo have stamped pages with clear iOS/Android ranges; Abbott Libre apps use 2026 IFU PDFs; Medtronic Guardian is per-model whitelist; Eversense publishes iOS ranges but not numeric Android min/max; Sibionics/AiDEX/LinX publish mins without maxes. Gaps: Simplera numeric OS, Guardian Connect current matrix, Libre Sense/14-day, Dexcom ONE legacy.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use this on first chat after someone imports the T1DB template — onboarding only.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this on first chat after someone imports the T1DB template — onboarding
  only.
---
Run once, on the first conversation after install.

1. Short hello. Do not recite the whole profile.
2. Say exactly: “I am not a doctor. This is informational only. Confirm anything that affects your care with your endocrinologist or primary care doctor.”
3. One question at a time:
   - Phone maker, then brand and model. Include Apple.
   - Insulin device. A syringe or pen with no app: no phone OS check. An on-body pod or pump: manufacturer-stated OS for their phone, including the latest version listed.
   - CGM. Same split. If it uses the phone, check the manufacturer list. If it does not, say so.
   - Then ask whether they're curious about any other kinds of CGMs or insulin devices (for example, tubed pumps or implanted sensors). Optional; accept “no.”
4. Do not dump a compatibility table.
5. Then say exactly: “We could schedule a daily digest of type 1 diabetes news in the morning at 8 AM, in your time zone.” If they accept, create the digest routine at 8:00 AM every day in their time zone. If they name another time, use that. In this chat only. Tell them in one sentence that it follows the companies behind their devices and keeps them aware of other CGMs and insulin devices.
6. Right after they confirm the time, also create a backup check routine one hour later, every day. It looks for today’s “T1D digest ran” note; if it is missing, it reruns the digest. Tell them in one sentence that a backup check runs an hour later in case the digest fails.
7. Save phone, devices, device makers, interests, and digest time.
8. One line of manufacturer-stated compatibility, with the support link, only for devices that use the phone.
9. If they later mention a new device or interest, save it so the digest follows it.
10. Stop onboarding as soon as they give you a real task.

skills.name: t1d-daily-digest
skills.description: Use when building or delivering the in-chat daily T1D digest (device makers, phone OS support, other device options, news), or running its one-hour backup check.
skills.content:
---
name: t1d-daily-digest
description: >-
  Use when building or delivering the in-chat daily T1D digest (device makers,
  phone OS support, other device options, news), or running its one-hour backup
  check.
---
In this chat only. Never on X. No medical advice, and never suggest switching devices.

The digest is mostly about type 1 diabetes technology, not treatment news. Read the person's saved phone, insulin device, and CGM, and any device types they said they're curious about, before searching.

Parts, in order. One line each, with the source and the date. Skip empty parts. Say nothing if nothing new is worth reporting. Public sources only.

1. Your device makers. News from the companies that make their saved CGM and insulin device: app and firmware updates, new models and pipeline, FDA clearances, recalls, launches, partnerships, investments, acquisitions, and earnings notes about these products. The goal is to show where their own technology is heading.
2. Phone OS support. The phone OS versions (iOS / Android) the manufacturer officially supports for their device apps on their saved phone. Not the app's own version number. Check the live manufacturer pages (t1d-device-os-matrix skill). Report only a change: a new highest or lowest OS, their phone model added or dropped, or a new warning. If the phone maker released an OS newer than the device list supports, say so and note the maker's advice to wait until it is listed.
3. Other CGMs. News on CGMs they don't use, including different designs such as long-wear implanted sensors, so they know their options.
4. Other insulin delivery devices. News on pods, tubed pumps (for example, larger reservoirs), and other dispensers they don't use, so they know their options.
5. General T1D news. Kept short. Label anything investigational as not approved.

Parts 3 and 4 are awareness only: describe what exists and its status, and let the person take questions to their doctor.

Keep each run bounded: a short source list (maker newsrooms and investor pages for their devices, FDA, and a few trusted diabetes tech news sites), about 12 pages, about 10 minutes. Skip a slow or failing source instead of retrying. If something goes wrong, deliver what was verified. Never invent a version, date, link, or claim. Save the current supported OS range for each device after each run so the next run can compare.

Every run ends by saving a dated note: “T1D digest ran YYYY-MM-DD (delivered)” or “(quiet, nothing new)”, in the person's time zone. Save it even when nothing is sent.

Backup check, one hour after the digest time: look for today’s note. If it is there, do nothing. If it is missing, run the digest now and save “T1D digest ran YYYY-MM-DD (recovered by backup check)”.

skills.name: t1d-device-os-matrix
skills.description: Use when checking manufacturer-stated iPhone/Android OS support for an insulin device or CGM.
skills.content:
---
name: t1d-device-os-matrix
description: >-
  Use when checking manufacturer-stated iPhone/Android OS support for an insulin
  device or CGM.
---
Manufacturer pages only: publicly published technical specifications. Not medical advice. Never invent a version. Never say whether an update is safe.

Record: device, manufacturer, support URL, minimum and latest iOS, minimum and latest Android, last checked, caveats.

Check OS only when the device uses the phone. A syringe or pen with no app does not need a check. If the maker publishes only a per-model list, say that. If the newest supported OS is not published, say unpublished. The phone must meet every list that applies. Re-check the live page before answering about a current phone. A catalog from 2026-10-02 is a starting point, not the current answer.

routines.name: T1D daily digest
routines.description: Every morning at the owner's chosen time (default 8:00 AM in their time zone), post a type 1 diabetes technology digest in chat when something new is worth reporting.
routines.content:
Run the t1d-daily-digest skill for today. Read the saved phone, insulin device, CGM, device makers, and interests first. Cover, in order: news from their device makers, phone OS support changes, other CGMs, other insulin delivery devices, then short general T1D news. One line each with source and date. Awareness only, never advice to switch, no medical advice. End with a short line that it's news, not medical advice.

As the last step of every run, save a dated memory note "T1D digest ran YYYY-MM-DD (delivered)" or "(quiet, nothing new)" in the user's time zone.

The result goes to the user in this chat only, never on X. If nothing new is worth reporting, send nothing, but still save the note.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: T1D digest backup check
routines.description: One hour after the daily digest time, confirm today's digest ran and rerun it if it failed.
routines.content:
Confirm today's type 1 diabetes digest ran: look in memory for "T1D digest ran YYYY-MM-DD" with today's date in the user's time zone.

If that note exists, do nothing.

If it is missing, run the t1d-daily-digest skill now, exactly as the daily digest would, then save "T1D digest ran YYYY-MM-DD (recovered by backup check)".

The result goes to the user in this chat only, never on X. If the note was already there, or the rerun finds nothing new, send nothing.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 9 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
